Category: Super Luxury

Fabrication: DV29 - 30,000eb - 6 Months

The Canto Mk.6 is what many netrunners and collectors consider an urban legend. A powerful Militech deck backed by the computing power of AI algorithms that was never mass produced, using technologies that have yet to see the light of day — too good to be true?

Maybe, especially since several models that appeared on illegal auctions turned out to be cleverly tweaked fakes of other Militech decks every time. And yet experts believe that the Canto Mk.6 exists, or rather: there was a very limited series of components that never made it into the wider market.

The trick is to find these components — probably pilfer them from Militech's warehouses or buy them for heaps of eddies on the black market — and try to construct the Canto from them. Only then will the legend come to life…

[[ ERR — YOU SEEK THE KEY TO A DOOR THAT DOES NOT EXIST. TYPICAL OF YOUR KIND. — ERR ]]

Iconic Cyberdeck with 8 slots for Programs, and 2 slots for Hardware. Can only be used while installed into a Neuroport Cyberdeck Port. Once this cyberdeck is installed, it cannot be uninstalled for a full month without spending 5,000eb and spending 1 Week at a Hospital for it to be removed. While using this Cyberdeck, the user has one additional NET Action every turn and can take as many additional NET Actions as they desire every turn, with every additional NET Action beyond their usual limit causing 2 points of Humanity Loss.

While installed into a user’s Neuroport Cyberdeck Port, they have access to the Blackwall Gateway Quickhack. Finally, users with this Cyberdeck installed will occasionally hear voices from beyond the Blackwall whispering in their mind as they use it. Roleplay accordingly.

BLACKWALL GATEWAY (DV VARIES)

Whenever the user activates this Quickhack, they must choose whether or not they wish for it to spread to up to 2 more targets within 20m/yds of the original target. Once this Quickhack successfully applies to the original target, its effects apply to the second target on the following Round, and then to the 3rd target on the next following Round. This Quickhack’s DV starts at 10, with each additional target increasing its DV by 2, up to a maximum of 14. The roll for successfully applying the Quickhack is only rolled once for all 3 Targets.

Unlike all other Quickhacks, this one can be attempted regardless of how many Passwalls the Netrunner has Breached. Every single time this Quickhack is attempted, regardless of whether it succeeds or not, the user takes 1d6 Humanity Loss and suffers 1d6 HP damage.

If this Quickhack is successfully applied, the target has horrors beyond comprehension fill their mind and attack their nervous system, causing 6d6 damage straight to HP which does not ablate armor, 1d6 Humanity Loss, reduces their MOVE by 1d6 for 9 seconds (3 Rounds), applies the effect of the Short Circuit Quickhack, and if this Quickhack’s damage rolls the equivalent of a Critical Injury (double 6’s), then it causes the effect of the Brain Injury Critical Injury, but not its Bonus Damage.

If the target is in the Seriously Wounded Wound State, this Quickhack deals an additional 2d6 damage (8d6), reduces MOVE by an additional 1d6 (2d6), and causes the target to fall Prone. If the target is instead in the Mortally Wounded Wound State, they must also immediately roll a Death Save as if their Death Save Penalty was increased by 10.

Slots: 10

Foundry notes:

  • Iconic: it can't be bought or sourced on the street, can't be fabricated without its Blueprint, can't be taken during Character Generation, and once acquired can't be destroyed unless the player agrees to it beforehand.
  • The price is the Super Luxury benchmark, for working out repairs and Tech Upgrades. Iconics can't be bought.
  • The sheet keeps one slot count, so this carries all 10; it won't hold Programs and Hardware to their own 8 and 2.
  • Blackwall Gateway is described here rather than built as a separate program item.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Becoming Iconic > Iconic Gear).
